Hi Alex — quick security answers below (bullet form for the marketplace doc). Happy to join call if you want verbatim language.

1) Data residency:
- Hosted Redwood Marketplace deployments support regional pinning per-customer. For AWS/GCP/Azure we can pin compute and storage to a specific cloud region (e.g., AWS us-east-1, GCP us-central1, Azure eastus).
- For Redwood Dedicated/Private installs we can deploy into customer VPCs or on-prem to meet strict residency needs.
- Note: logs related to control-plane telemetry (for billing/health) are configurable and can be routed to customer-owned logging endpoints; we can exclude sensitive payloads from control-plane collectors on request.

2) Retention defaults and controls:
- Default request logs retention: 90 days.
- Model inputs (raw payloads): default 30 days; customers can opt-in to longer retention for debugging/ML workflows.
- KV cache artifacts (ephemeral): retained for 0-7 days depending on workload; we offer TTL controls per-model.
- Customers can override retention via Console (per-route retention policy) or via API for programmatic compliance; enterprise contracts can set custom retention windows.

3) Deletion and evidence:
- Deletion workflow: customer requests deletion via console/API or via written request to support; we execute a two-phase purge (service layer deletion, followed by storage scrub) and post a deletion ticket.
- SLA: standard deletion execution within 30 days for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private we commit to contract-specific timelines (often 7–14 days).
- Evidence: we can provide exportable deletion tickets, audit logs showing deletion events (timestamps, operator IDs), and a signed affidavit for enterprise procurement if required.

Attachments to share: redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf (detailed table by artifact), redwood-soc2-extracts.zip (SOC 2 report excerpts).

Let me know if you need exact phrasing for the marketplace UI or a sample affidavit.

Alex — adding a small marketplace-specific note: Cloud marketplaces often require a region mapping table so buyers understand where compute will run. I've attached a quick spreadsheet that maps Redwood deployment choices to common marketplace region enums. Important operational notes:

- For AWS listings we recommend specifying both a primary (e.g., us-east-1) and a compatible fallback region (us-west-2) to avoid listing rejection when capacity constraints occur.
- For Azure/GCP, the marketplace listing should call out that "US-region" deployments will be restricted to named regions (we will list the exact regions in the listing detail).
- If CloudMart procurement requires that backups also remain in-region, we should include that in the listing; by default backups follow compute region but we can provide explicit backup residency on request.

Attachment: marketplace-region-mapping.xlsx

Happy to produce the single-slide summary for the listing page. Jasmine — can you confirm preferred language for the listing bullet: "Data residency: Customer data and backups remain in selected US cloud regions; control-plane telemetry can be routed to customer-owned endpoints on request."
